Every quoted item checked against the page images and found as quoted: 1 abaká, 2 pugáp, 3 námin, 11 bollók, 13 dupá?, 14 kú…
new_statements.relation_note: new: nothing on record for pudt1235. Data-only evidence (per-item accent marks in an unpublished SIL survey wordlist), not a stated rule. For the sister language Pamplona Atta, Whittle & Lusted 1963: 28 (held in this folder) state 'primary stress on the ultima' with pitch-marked secondary stress on long vowels; the Pudtol list's sizeable penult minority is a different variety's data, not a contradiction of anything on record.
new_statements.translation_language: Pudtol Atta forms with English list header
new_statements.rule_in_words: No rule is stated; this is a survey wordlist. Every filled item carries one typed acute accent, which falls on the final syllable in roughly three quarters of the marked forms and on the penult in most of the rest (approximate count from the text-layer glyph coordinates: c. 120 ultima vs c. 39 penult, a handful earlier; checker B's independent estimate was c. 115 vs 33); both positions occur on words of the same shape (bukú, kapá?, dagá?, utá? vs ítu, gáta?, úta, bággi), i.e. the transcription treats stress position as a lexical property (final vs penult), as in neighbouring Ibanag. Reading inferred from transcription marks only, hence low confidence.
new_statements.secondary_stress: none marked; no separate vowel-length notation seen in this list (the sister Annip list writes length with a colon)
new_statements.identity_note: Nickell 1981 (SIL 77317) is Pudtol Atta proper: San Jose, Pudtol (Apayao), 'Panamon project', speaker Inggol Lagimon of Libawa, San Jose (wife from Luna). Headland 2003 lists 'Atta, Pudtol, Kalinga-Apayao' (pop. 100) beside Pamplona and Faire-Rizal Atta. The Faire/Bullakit/Annip lists (SIL 77207, 77208, 77200) are Faire Atta [azt] and the Rizal variety; the 1966 Pamplona list (Reid 1971) and Whittle & Lusted 1963 are Pamplona Atta [att].

sources.note: Sec. 2.1 (p. 28): the word is the unit bounded by potential pause and 'marked by primary stress on the ultima'; primary stress = volume on a low pitch ('a low push'); secondary stress with a pitch rise falls on long vowels and sounds like primary stress to American ears. Sec. 1/2.3 (pp. 27, 30): a prosodeme of length, contrastive on a, i, u (e, o always long), only on the second vowel of a cluster; length also a plural morpheme (abbing/a:bbing) and intonational. Sec. 3.6 (pp. 38-39): source-language stressed vowels in Spanish loans become long vowels 'which in Atta have secondary stress concu…
No descriptive references: only Reid 2006 (subclassification comment) and Ethnologue. Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology.
